title: A 30-person backyard birthday party on a $400 budget
summary: A celebratory $400 plan for 30 people: food, drinks, decor, and a contingency that still feels like a party.

blocks.title: Thirty people, four hundred dollars, one backyard
blocks.body: This is a working budget for a casual afternoon birthday — grill food, drinks, simple decor, and music from a speaker you already own. Numbers are example targets you can swap.

blocks.heading: Budget map
rows: Burgers/dogs, buns, salad, chips, fruit, condiments
Water, lemonade, a small cooler of sodas; BYOB optional for adults
Grocery sheet cake or cupcakes + candles
Plates, cups, napkins, balloons, one banner
Bags of ice, trash bags, wet wipes
Forgot mustard, extra ice, last-minute chairs
blocks.caption: Totals $400. Slide money from decor into food if your crowd is hungrier than fancy.

blocks.heading: Food plan that feeds 30 without catering prices

items.label: Main: burgers + hot dogs (plan ~1.25 servings/person)
items.detail: Buy patties and dogs on sale; freeze extras the day before if needed.

items.label: Sides: big bowl salad, chips, cut fruit
items.detail: Two large sides beat six tiny fancy ones on this budget.

items.label: Dessert: one sheet cake, first-name on it
Ask two friends to bring a side each
items.detail: Keeps the host budget honest without turning it into a potluck free-for-all.

items.title: Shop + chill drinks
items.detail: Buy non-perishables, ice chests ready, playlist queued.

items.title: Yard + tables
items.detail: Mow path, set tables, hang banner, stage trash/recycle.

items.title: Food prep
items.detail: Paties formed, sides chopped, cake in fridge, cooler packed.

items.title: Grill open, drinks iced
items.detail: Host works the grill; a friend runs the drink cooler.

items.title: Soft landing
items.detail: Trash run, leftover plan, thank-you texts later — not during cleanup.

columns.name: Keep
columns.detail: Enough food, cold drinks, a named cake, somewhere to sit, a clear trash plan.

columns.name: Cut first
columns.detail: Theme decor kits, custom napkins, rented bounce house, professional photographer, multiple meat options.

blocks.title: Tone check
blocks.body: A $400 backyard party wins on warmth and enough food, not on Instagram props. Put the money where guests feel it: grill smoke, cold lemonade, and a cake with the right name.

blocks.heading: Tonight
blocks.body: Write the six budget lines on a sticky note. Invite with a clear end time. Ask two people to bring sides. Protect the $30 contingency like it is sacred.
